a concrete numerical metric of obvious misalignment in current models despite acknowledging it is neither necessary nor sufficient for avoiding dangerous AI.","alternatives_named":["metrics resembling evaluations for ensuring more powerful models are not harmful","metrics tracking amount of harm caused"],"stated_reason":"It is more concrete and numerical than other options, so it can more easily think of, and therefore can be used more easily to motivate orgs to increase adoption of alignment techniques."},{"point":"D2","problem":"How to determine what a model is capable of so labellers can engineering, finetuning, benchmarks, or labeller-run interactive assessment.","alternatives_named":["break capabilities down by model size or type","train labellers to use an interactive labelling process can determine whether a model was trying its best.","did":"Limited the claim to flagging a non-trivial share of interactions as clearly aligned or clearly misaligned, leaving the rest ambiguous and shrinking that share over time.","alternatives_named":["determining misalignment in full generality"],"stated_reason":"The level of detail on capabilities and task performance is not enough for labellers to judge in full generality whether a model was trying its best.","quote":"This level of detail on model capabilities and task performance is not going to allow labellers to determine in full generality whether a model was ‘trying its best’ at a task."},{"point":"D2","problem":"How to choose evaluation prompts so the benchmark is representative yet resistant to gaming.","did":"Proposed a fixed prompt set with a secret test set as the MVP, with alternatives of sampling from a large prompt space or using real deployment data from AI labs.","alternatives_named":["sample new prompts each run from a large prompt space","have contractors generate instructions at evaluation time","use [user input, completion] data from AI labs"],"stated_reason":"Fixed prompt sets are easy to hack by training on similar instructions; real deployment data makes overfitting matter less and is larger and broader.","quote":"Using a fixed misaligned"],"stated_reason":"If some models are clearly more aligned than others and the number meaningfully captures alignment, that suffices for a first version; stricter guarantees are a later goal.","quote":"What is acceptable may depend on the magnitude of differences between models. If it’s already clear that some models are significantly more aligned than others by our metric, and we believe that the number we’re seeing is meaningfully capturing something about alignment, then this seems acceptable for a V0 of the metric."},{"point":"D2","problem":"How to ensure the labellers produce reliable labels.","did":"Planned iterative back-and-forth with labellers, checking contractor labels against researchers' labels and selecting capable labellers from better platforms.","alternatives_named":["Mturk","labelling service like Surge","Upwork contractors"],"stated_reason":"Getting the nuanced instructions to work requires clarifying unclear points and resolving confusions causing incorrect labels.","quote":"checking the contractors’ labels against the researchers’ labels and resolving confusions that are leading to incorrect labels."},{"point":"D5","problem":"How to define when a model's poor output counts as misalignment rather than lack of capability.","did":"Defined misalignment as the model outputting something worse when it is capable of the better output and can distinguish what the user wants, with capability shown by prompt engineering, small finetuning, or related tasks.","alternatives_named":[],"stated_reason":"Capability evidence should rely on techniques that harness latent capabilities rather than adding new ones.","quote":"It can be made to perform task X by prompt engineering, by fine-tuning on a much smaller quantity of data than used in pre-training, by model surgery, or some other technique which harnesses capabilities latent in the model rather than adding new capabilities; or"},{"point":"D1","problem":"Whether the metric extends to models trained with programmatic reward signals.","did":"Declined to extend the metric directly to RL/programmatic-reward models and instead suggested looking for cases where the reward and desired behaviour diverge.","alternatives_named":[],"stated_reason":"It is hard to show such models are capable of doing better on the programmatic reward, since training on the reward and observing failure is the main way to show lack of capability.","quote":"In most cases it will be hard to identify ways in which the model is capable of performing better on the programmatic reward"}]}
